_meta.feast: Holy Hierarch Abercius, Bishop of Hierapolis & the Seven Youths of Ephesus
_meta._note: Two interleaved festal canons: Canon I of Abercius (Joseph, Tone II) + Canon II of the Seven Youths of Ephesus (Tone VIII). Kontakion of the Seven Youths (Tone IV, with ikos) at after-Ode-3 slot; Kontakion of Abercius (Tone VIII, with ikos) at standard after-Ode-6 slot. Two exapostilaria. Sessional hymns: Abercius Tone VIII + Seven Youths Tone IV (Glory) + Theotokion Tone IV. KNOWN GAP: Matins Aposticha empty pending weekday Octoechos scrape.

troparion.text: The truth of things revealed thee to thy flock as a rule of faith, * icon of meekness, and teacher of temperance; * wherefore, thou hast attained the heights through humility and riches through poverty; * O hierarch Abercius our father, ** entreat Christ God, that our souls be saved.
troparion.label: Troparion of St. Abercius the Hierarch

kontakion.text: The whole Church of the faithful doth reckon thee * to be a most excellent priest and dweller with the apostles, O Abercius. * By thy supplications preserve it invincible, un-assailed and undefiled by all heresy, ** in that thou art ever-memorable.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of St. Abercius

sessionalHymns.text: Thou hast been shown to be a hierarch anointed with precious oils in a godly manner, O most sacred and all-praised father Abercius, working all things through grace, adorned with the splendor of divine gifts and miracles, healing sicknesses, burning up the demons, converting multitudes of the deluded. Wherefore, we cry out to thee: Entreat Christ God, that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love.
sessionalHymns.label: Sessional Hymn of St. Abercius (after Ode 3)

sessionalHymns.text: As pillars of the Church of Christ ye mightily destroyed the walls of unbelief, O seven martyred brethren; wherefore, before your death ye destroyed the rage of the heathen, and after your death ye destroyed the storm of heresy, pray ye for our souls.
sessionalHymns.label: Glory — Sessional Hymn of the Seven Youths of Ephesus

sessionalHymns.text: O pure, all-immaculate one who knewest not a man, who alone hast given birth within time to the timeless Son and Word of God, with the holy and honored patriarchs, the martyrs, prophets and the venerable, entreat Him, that He grant us purification and great mercy.
sessionalHymns.label: Both now — Theotokion

troparion.text: The truth of things revealed thee to thy flock as a rule of faith, * icon of meekness, and teacher of temperance; * wherefore, thou hast attained the heights through humility and riches through poverty; * O hierarch Abercius our father, ** entreat Christ God, that our souls be saved.
troparion.label: Troparion of St. Abercius the Hierarch

canon._authors: Canon I of Abercius by Joseph in Tone II + Canon II of the Seven Youths of Ephesus in Tone VIII. Octoechos canons omitted.

kontakionAfterOde3.text: O Christ Who hast glorified Thy saints on earth, * before Thine awesome Second Coming * Thou hast shown forth the resurrection to those who knew it not, * through the most glorious raising up of the youths, * revealing their clothing and bodies as incorrupt; * prevailing upon the emperor to cry aloud: ** Truly there is resurrection for the dead!
kontakionAfterOde3.label: Kontakion of the Seven Youths of Ephesus

ikos.text: When the bishop of Ephesus beheld the wondrous and exalted resurrection of the youths, astonished in mind he wrote with haste to the most faithful emperor, describing their arising: "May thy highness deign to come hither, O master, that thou mayest see the power of our God, which He hath shown to thee." And rising up straightway, the great victor made the journey, rejoicing, showing himself to be another charioteer like Elijah, crying aloud: Truly there is resurrection for the dead!

kontakion.text: The whole Church of the faithful doth reckon thee * to be a most excellent priest and dweller with the apostles, O Abercius. * By thy supplications preserve it invincible, un-assailed and undefiled by all heresy, ** in that thou art ever-memorable.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of St. Abercius

ikos.text: Mindful of the vanity of this world, as a stranger to the world and an emulator of the suffering of Christ thou didst mortify the carnal passions, and taking up thy cross, O blessed one, thou didst follow after thy Creator. Abiding with Him now, pray thou for those who truly honor thee, in that thou art ever-memorable.

ode1.irmos:
Come, O ye people, let us sing a song to Christ our God,
Who divided the sea, and made a way for the nation which He had brought up out of the bondage of Egypt;//
for He hath been glorified.
ode1.irmos2:
The wonderworking staff of Moses,
striking and dividing the sea in the figure of a cross,
once drowned Pharaoh the pursuing charioteer,
while it saved the fleeing people of Israel as they fled on foot,
chanting a hymn unto God.

troparia.text: Illumined with the radiant splendor of the three-Sunned Godhead, O Abercius, thou didst become a light enlightening those in darkness and dispelling all the darkness of the demons.
Thou didst lead a heavenly life on earth, O most blessed one, living in the flesh as one of the incorporeal ones and mortifying the passions; thereby receiving the gift of the priesthood.
Having within thyself the gift of preaching, O father, thou didst destroy the irrationality of the vain-minded, casting down the temples of the demons and their false graven images.

Theotokion: The tongues of orators are at a loss how to describe thy conceiving, which is beyond all telling; for thou hast given birth to God in the flesh, O all-pure one, Who in His goodness became like unto us.

O ye seven holy youths, who are honored by the number seven, ye radiant stars shining in the firmament of the Church, who by your witness have come to dwell in the heavens: be ye mindful of those who honor you with faith.

Forming a lamp of sevenfold brilliance with the sevenfold radiance of the Spirit, O ye seven martyrs, ye caused the darkness of delusion to diminish, and with the light of piety ye now illumine us all with a sevenfold radiance.
Theotokion: On thee, O Virgin, do I place my hope of salvation: wash from me all the mire of sin and make me pure, that I may be well-pleasing to thy Son and do His all-holy will.

ode3.irmos:
O Lord, who didst slay sin upon the tree,
firmly establish us in Thee,
and in the hearts of us who hymn Thee plant the fear of Thee.
ode3.irmos2:
O Christ fortify me on the rock of Thy commandments,
Thou who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding
and didst establish the earth upon the waters,
for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind.

troparia.text: By sacred words and the performing of miracles, O Abercius, thou hast most gloriously guided those who sail the sea of deception to the calm haven of salvation.
Working healings, performing excellent miracles and dispelling the fantasies of the demons, thou hast been the cause of salvation for all and an intercessor for the rich.
O father, thy discourse was sacred, thy life godly, thy character resplendent with miracles, thy manner of living glorious, and thy death honorable.
Theotokion: God Who before was invisible became visible, O Virgin, being incarnate of thy womb in His compassion; wherefore, we bless thee with faith.

Appearing on earth in sevenfold radiance like lamps of the virtues, and shining brightly in the effulgence of your struggles and the brilliance of your miracles, ye have shone the light of the knowledge of God upon the whole world.
Offered to the Creator from earliest infancy, for His sake ye spurned glory, royal honors and transitory riches, for which ye have received the glory of incorruptible honors.
Theotokion: With the activity of the Life which appeared through thee to the world, O only most immaculate Birthgiver of God, raise up my deadened mind, destroying the wounds and types of sin.

ode4.irmos:
I hymn Thee, O Lord, for I have heard report of Thee, and I was afraid;
for Thou comest to me, seeking me who am lost.
Wherefore, I glorify Thy great condescension towards me,
O greatly Merciful One.
ode4.irmos2:
Thou, O Lord, art my strength and Thou art my power,
Thou art my God and Thou art my joy,
Thou Who, while never leaving the bosom of Thy Father, hast visited our poverty.
Therefore with the Prophet Habbakuk I cry unto Thee,
'Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!'

troparia.text: Thou didst abundantly adorn thy cathedra, O venerable hierarch, rendering it utterly magnificent with great miracles and a splendid life; wherefore, our God hath greatly glorified thee.
Knowing that the Lord desireth mercy, O God-bearer, thou didst beseech Him fervently to cause a most wondrous outpouring of fervent waters for the healing and salvation of many.

By the grace of God thou didst make childless women fertile, fulfilling their intentions; for having manifestly sown upon them thy words as seed, O blessed Abercius, like a good sower thou didst reap grain a hundredfold.

Theotokion: O all-immaculate Bride of God thou hast healed the contrition and ancient accursedness of mortals, having given birth to Christ, the King and Lord, Who hath taken upon Himself our infirmities in His ineffable compassion.

Bound together with a fraternal bond, and set afire with divine desire, O martyrs of the Lord, ye agreed on making a true confession of faith and thereby put to shame the vain-minded understanding of the tyrants and the false teaching of polytheism.

Persecuted for Christ and with Christ, hiding in caves and mountainous wastelands, instead of death, for many long years ye slept a life-bearing sleep for His sake, clearly confirming the general resurrection of mortals.

Theotokion: That in the richness of Thy goodness Thou mightest restore Thine image which had become dim through the passions, Thou didst make Thine abode within the Virgin's womb, making it wisdom, the temple of God, through which thou didst come to dwell with mankind and save the ends of the world, O Compassionate One.

ode5.irmos:
O Christ my Savior, the enlightenment of those lying in the darkness of sin,
I rise early to hymn Thee O King of Peace,
enlighten me with Thy radiance,
for I know no other God than Thee.
ode5.irmos2:
O Light never-waning,
why hast Thou turned Thy face from me
and why hath the alien darkness surrounded me, wretched though I be?
But do Thou guide my steps I implore Thee
and turn me back towards the light of Thy commandments.

troparia.text: Having set thy feet upon the rock of thy heart, O divinely wise and blessed one, with divine words thou didst teach those who had fallen into perdition rendered worship to stones, such that they worshiped the Rock, Jesus Christ our God.

Let us honor Abercius the teacher of sacred things, the excellent physician of the infirm, the guide of all who have been deceived by evil counsel, the phial of precious gifts, the receptacle of the divine Spirit.

When wine and oil were placed together in a single vessel and mixed together at thy command, at the appointed time they were poured forth most gloriously unmingled, manifestly revealing thy most excellent grace, O sacred one.

Theotokion: In thee, O Virgin, are the laws of nature most gloriously restored; for without seed thou didst give birth to God the Savior, and remained a virgin — O the awesome wonder! Wherefore, we piously declare thee to be the Mother of Emmanuel.

Having died to the world, ye rejected all the beauties of life, committing your life to Him Who hath dominion over life, and slept a life-bearing sleep for many years as an image of the general resurrection.
Enduring long persecution, ye showed yourselves to be spiritual athletes by your life, bearing hunger and thirst and divers tribulations, sorrows and misfortunes, yet made rich in tranquility.

Theotokion: Made rich in thee, our rampart, and protected by thine intercession, boasting in thy divine glory, we call thee blessed; for thou, O most holy one, dost pour forth gladness and joy upon our souls.

ode6.irmos:
Whirled about in the abyss of sin,
I appeal to the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion:
Raise me up from corruption, O God.

troparia.text: Thou didst go from the East to the West, O venerable one, driving away the queen of demonic and cruel passion by the power of the Spirit.
Thou didst appear strange to the world, O most sacred Abercius, working wondrous and awesome miracles, walking in the body and departing therefrom.
Seen to be as bright as lightning, O divinely inspired father Abercius, thou didst vanquish hordes of the demons, who were unable to bear the threat of thee.
Theotokion: Through thee, O all-holy Bride of God, we, who are dead, have been deemed worthy of life, and we who are in thrall to corruption have manifestly been enriched by incorruption.
With love for God, O wise ones, ye left your Ephesians' homeland, your splendid family, illustrious riches and honorable glory, preferring to inherit heaven.
The seven-member choir of spiritual athletes, joining together in a godly manner, cast down the manifold multitude of the enemy and received the glory of confession, and crowns for their suffering.
Theotokion: The majesty of the Most High shone forth from Sion, arrayed through a union in the flesh which He received from thee who knewest not wedlock; and He hath thereby enlightened the world.

ode7.irmos:
When the golden image was worshipped on the plain of Dura,
Thy three children spurned the impious command,
and, cast into the midst of the flame,
they were bedewed, and sang:
O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

troparia.text: As a godly shepherd, as a performer of miracles, O father, by thy prayer thou hast granted the blind to see and the deaf to hear, and bestowed cleansing upon lepers, and the ability to walk to the lame, who chant: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

The bubbling spring of warm water and the pillar which lieth on thy grave, which the wicked spirit, driven out by thee, O father Abercius, carried back from great Rome, proclaim thine ability to work miracles throughout the ages.

Thou wast a guide for the humble, having been revealed as exalted in vision and activity and power, O most sacred one, as a favorite of the most high King. To Him do we cry: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

Theotokion: He Who was begotten of the Father before the morning-star was born from thee in two natures and wills, as both God and man, O Maiden, and is known to all who cry out with faith: Blessed art thou who hast given birth to God in the flesh!

Submitting to God, and guided by divine law and an upright mind, ye set at naught the exceedingly wicked commands of the tormentors, O youths, acquiring life and incorruption through death, enriched in your mortal bodies.

Desiring to drink the cup of death for the Creator with faith, for the sake of immortality and incorruption ye endured the burial of your bodies, making plain the resurrection by your most glorious rising from the dead, O martyrs.

Theotokion: Thou didst shine forth like the morning, having the Sun of righteousness Who, through divine knowledge, taketh away the darkness of ignorance from the world. To Him do we chant, O most pure one: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou!

ode8.irmos:
God Who descended into the fiery furnace with the Hebrew children,
and transformed the flame into dew,
do ye works hymn,
and supremely exalt as Lord throughout all ages.
ode8.irmos2:
In his wrath the Chaldean Tyrant made the furnace blaze,
with heat fanned sevenfold for the servants of God;
but when he perceived that they had been saved by a greater power
he cried aloud to the Creator and Redeemer:
'ye children bless, ye priests praise,
ye people, supremely exalt Him throughout all ages.'

troparia.text: Let Abercius be honored as a most glorious shepherd, an inexhaustible well-spring of healings, a pillar of the Church, the confirmation of the faithful, a great luminary and a most splendid teacher of sacred things.

Like the palm-tree of the psalms thou didst flourish in the courts of the living God; multiplying like the cedar, O wise one, and wast revealed to be like an olive-tree, causing the faces of all to shine with faith through the oil of thy works.

Through thine active life, thou wast manifestly known to be like a city standing on the summit of a mountain, O venerable one; and thy city, which of old was sunk in deception, thou hast revealed to be like an heir to the city of the Most High.

Theotokion: Behold, the bridal-couch of Solomon, surrounded now by the mighty prophecies of the divinely inspired Scriptures, and one upon which Christ God hath rested in His divine incarnation, O blessed and joyous one.

Your memory hath shone forth with a sevenfold radiance today like the beams of the sun, illumining the earth with the splendors of your suffering, with the brilliance of your miracles, and with the rays of divine dogmas wherewith ye assure all of the resurrection of the body and the incorruption of mortals, O wise ones.

Once, God preserved Abimelech in the field, that he might not see the destruction of Jerusalem; and He preserved you asleep for a great many years in the cave as an assurance of the resurrection of all, O youths, ye lamps equal in number to the seven ages.

Theotokion: Sanctified by the Spirit, O all-immaculate Theotokos, thou didst truly receive the beginningless and everlasting Son in thy womb, Who became incarnate within thee, O pure one, for the benefaction of those who cry out with faith: Ye children bless; ye priests hymn; ye people supremely exalt Him throughout all ages.

ode9.irmos:
God the Word, God of God,
Who by ineffable wisdom came to create Adam anew
after his grievous fall to corruption through eating
and Who took flesh beyond all telling from the Holy Virgin for our sake,
Him we faithful with one accord magnify in song.
ode9.irmos2:
Heaven was stricken with awe,
and the ends of the earth were filled with amazement,
for God hath appeared in the flesh,
and thy womb was rendered more spacious than the heavens.
Wherefore, the ranks of men and of angels
magnify thee as the Theotokos.

troparia.text: In that thy life was splendid and thy feet beautiful, in that thy yearning for God and neighbor was exceedingly wondrous, in that the grace given thee from on high was magnificent, O wise Abercius, we honor thee with faith.

With faith let us glorify thee, O Abercius, as one who dwelleth with all the holy martyrs, an emulator of the divine disciples, a peer of the patriarchs, prophets and the venerable, and a converser with the ministers of heaven.

Thy most holy memory, which extendeth throughout the world, doth illumine the souls of all with the rich light of grace. By thy supplications, O Abercius, deliver us who celebrate it with love from the passions and from perilous darkness, we pray thee.

Theotokion: The prophet beheld thee beforehand as a radiant lampstand bearing within thee as a truly divine Lamp the only transcendent God Who, in the compassion of His mercy, became man through thee, O all-holy Virgin.

Everyone born on earth marveled at this, and every mind was amazed, that mortals who lay buried for many years in a cave appeared as though having slept for an evening, rising up in the morning as was their wont, assuring all of the general resurrection of mortals.

O ye seven radiant luminaries and martyrs, ever-radiant beacons of Ephesus, intercessors for the whole world, fervent advocates, preachers of the general resurrection and guardians of the faithful: ask for us tranquility and salvation, and peace for all the ends of the world.

Theotokion: As thou art the Mother of Him Who suffered for us, in that thou art full of tender compassion, deliver me from soul-corrupting passions, and break thou the bonds of my transgressions. In that thou art good, bless now my soul, which is vexed by the assaults of demons, O Virgin Theotokos, that I may hymn thee, the all-hymned one.

exapostilarion.text: The hindering demon compelled thee to hasten to the city of Rome, for he had entered wickedly into the daughter of the emperor, O divinely eloquent Abercius; but thou didst drive him from her like a dog, compelling him to carry a pillar back to Hierapolis.
exapostilarion.label: Exapostilarion of St. Abercius

glory.text: Thy spiritual athletes, O Lord, protecting themselves with the weapon of Thy precious Cross, mightily vanquished the adverse powers, put the tyrants to shame and suffered for Thee; and they reign together with Thee, O my Christ, Thou King of all.
glory.label: Glory — Exapostilarion of the Seven Youths

bothnow.text: O thy mysteries! O thy wonders! How is it that even after giving birth thou didst remain a virgin as thou wast before birthgiving? How didst thou contain God Who is in nowise confined? Truly ineffable are all thy works, O blessed Mary!
bothnow.label: Both now — Theotokion
